title: Step by step of my chewy vanilla sugar cookies! I might forget every ...
description: Step by step of my chewy vanilla sugar cookies! I might forget every step of the way but FYI I made a double batch here - and you’ll want to also because this is one or my favorite recipes. Literally tastes like a grown up slice and bake with extra vanilla and the perfect amount of sweetness. You can find the full recipe on my website, and I’m also sharing ingredients for a double batch (18 cookies) below! 16 tablespoons (226g) unsalted butter, room temperature  1 cup (192g) granulated sugar  1 cup (120g) powdered sugar  2 large eggs, room temperature 2 teaspoons vanilla extract 2 teaspoons vanilla bean paste optional 3 cups (360g) all purpose flour    1 teaspoon baking soda 1/2 teaspoon baking powder 1/2 teaspoon salt 18 cookies, 34 carbs per cookie (for my fellow dia-bakers who need)  #bakingtutorial #sugarcookies #typefoodie #fyp
transcript: Let's bake my chewy vanilla sugar cookies. I'm gonna make a double batch since this recipe only makes, the original recipe only makes nine cookies. So first we'll go in with our butter. This is not sponsored, but I love Plupra. Then we're gonna go in with our sugars. This recipe uses granulated sugar and powdered sugar. Okay, I thought I added too much sugar, but we're doing a double batch so I'm gonna have to do some math. Okay, we're good. We're gonna let that go for a few minutes. Don't do what I did and put your mixer on high. As you start to see the butter and sugars like coming together, then you can bring it up high. And what I usually like to do is do that for like a couple of seconds and bring it down lower. Make sure we're good, and then you can let it run. It's been about a minute. We're gonna scrape down our attachment the sides of your mixing bowl and like make sure to get down to the bottom. We're gonna go back in for like another minute before we add more ingredients. All right, so now what we're seeing is like a much lighter color. It's fluffy, pretty nicely cream. Next, we're gonna add in our eggs. Again, I'm doing a double batch. So two eggs for me and then vanilla extract and also vanilla bean paste. So that's what gives this cookie. It's like a beautiful vanilla flavor. I do two teaspoons of our classic vanilla extract. Two teaspoons of the vanilla bean paste. These don't have to be like warm. Ideally you want all of your ingredients to be the same temperature. So since you're using room temperature butter, it's good to use room temperature eggs too. We're gonna mix again for another few minutes. Okay, so we're gonna go back to our scale and we're gonna add in our flour. If you don't use a kitchen scale, I highly recommend it. I often find flour is where things can go awry. So I really like using it for this especially. And we're gonna go ahead with baking soda, baking powder and salt. We're gonna mix again, but this is gonna be at our slowest speed. When we reach this shaggy dough consistency that you can see here, see some flour in there. Again, I like to come in with my spatula because there are some dry ingredients that are sticking to the side. You wanna make sure you're not missing any, especially a bit like baking powder, baking soda. I'm gonna keep going again at that really low speed. So now you can start to see it like ever so slightly sticking to the sides and I see a dough ball forming in the center. So that's when I'm gonna stop it. That looks good. Give it just like one more mix to make sure we didn't miss anything, especially down at the bottom. So this is what our finished dough looks like. I'm gonna scoop it and then I'm gonna put it in the fridge to chill. Now the dough has chilled for 30 minutes. It's a little bit more firm. Give it a squeeze and roll it between my palms so that we get a smooth exterior to the dough. Now that these are all rolled, they're gonna get covered in plastic wrap and I'm gonna put them in the fridge overnight. Now I'm gonna space out my chilled dough balls and bake them. I'll shape my baked cookies to make sure they're perfectly round and then let them chill. Okay, now they've chilled. So I'm gonna put them in a container and then put them in the fridge to keep them fresh. You can see the specks of vanilla, the golden brown bottom. These cookies are perfect. They're thick and chewy in the center and they'll stay fresh for days in the fridge.
